correctness.rationale: Rooted-forest determinant det(NI−J)=hN^(N−h−1) enumerates all trees containing a fixed k-edge path. Deleting prescribed offpath leaves and q path endpoints gives an exact count (s−q)(n−r−q)^(n−s−1), including s=n and s=q boundary cases. Dividing, binomial-inclusion expanding, and summing singleton terms gives the complete conditional leaf law and mean. Factoring adjacent means gives sign exactly 2(n−1)−k(k+1)^2. Strict increase of the cubic proves at most one change, and its real root is (2n)^(1/3)(1+o(1)). The included independently enumerating checker tested 280391 trees and 11214 rational assertions for finite cases; proof is analytic.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The level-by-level degree enumerator of Bousquet-Mélou–Chapuy (2012) is broad enough to encode the joint leaf/distance law by summing profiles after marking an individual target at level k. It is explicitly acknowledged as possible broader coverage of the enumeration ingredient. The signed cubic first-difference and unique n^(1/3) regression peak require an additional explicit evaluation and are absent from the inspected specializations. The 2003 Wiener-index abstract concerns distance-related moments, not a stated full conditional leaf regression. The endpoint-only published record does not by itself imply off-path total leaves.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Cayley rooted-forest enumeration immediately counts trees containing a fixed marked path; requiring additional offpath leaves yields the new finite-law simplification. The central new theorem is the exact global total-leaf conditional expectation and its sharp cubic reversal. Historical priority remains a nonzero risk, especially where complete prior texts were inaccessible.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The published endpoint-degree/distance theorem yields the one-endpoint-leaf event and therefore covers that special case. It does not, in its publicly readable summary, cover the global total-leaf conditional expectation or its cubic rise-to-fall boundary; these are the precise new claims. Remmel–Williamson gives unconditioned leaf-set counts. The fully inspected rooted-height/offspring counts of Bousquet-Mélou–Chapuy are more general input from which a joint distribution could be obtained by summation, but the sharp regression sign transition is not stated in the inspected statements. An uninspected equivalent priority source remains possible.

originality.rationale: A bounded examination of public primary sources and semantic research records found the exact global leaf-distance regression and its discrete cubic turning point unreported, although the single-endpoint conditional law is published and a broader depth/offspring enumerator gives possible algebraic coverage of the joint probability ingredient. The contribution is specifically the sharp sign transition and n^(1/3) maximizer, not rooted-forest counts, generic unconditioned leaf enumeration, or one endpoint leaf probability. The status is a self-review with documented priority risks, not independent verification.
residual_risks: A general degree-by-level enumeration by Bousquet-Mélou and Chapuy encodes joint leaf/distance statistics after summation; the explicit sharp turning point could be derivable, despite not appearing in the inspected theorems.
The full text of the published endpoint-degree/distance result was unavailable; only its public summary was compared, so stronger implied global statistics cannot be ruled out.
Some older random-tree literature, including the 2003 Wiener-index paper, was only available at abstract level. Targeted searches cannot certify priority.

value.rationale: Total leaves is a global branching statistic and fixed-pair distance is a natural geometric statistic of a uniform random spanning tree. Their conditional expectation is unexpectedly nonmonotone despite the previously known monotone endpoint-degree regression. The exact unique integer cubic threshold (including plateaus) and peak on a rare n^(1/3) path-length scale are natural, self-contained dependence information not evident from either marginal law or the older leaf-set counts.
